inline_comments.comment: `createLabel` is now `async` but `getClusterTitleWidth` is not — it calls `createLabel(...)` without `await`, so `label` is a `Promise`, not a DOM element. The subsequent `elem.node().appendChild(label)` and `label.getBBox()` will fail silently or throw at runtime. The function needs to be made `async` and the call must be `await`ed, with callers updated accordingly.

In the SVG (non-HTML) code path, `style.replace('color:', 'fill:')` is called unconditionally, but `style` can be `undefined` or `null` (e.g., when called from `clusters.js` with an unstyled node). This will throw a TypeError at runtime. The HTML path already guards with `style ? style.replace(...) : style`; the same guard must be applied here:
```js
svgLabel.setAttribute('style', style ? style.replace('color:', 'fill:') : '');
```

Same issue as in `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`: `style.replace('color:', 'fill:')` in the SVG path has no null guard. `style` can be `undefined`, causing a runtime TypeError. Apply the same guard used in the HTML path.

The original code checked `getConfig()?.htmlLabels` (the top-level global flag), but this line now checks `getConfig()?.flowchart?.htmlLabels` (the diagram-specific, deprecated flag). This silently ignores the global `htmlLabels` setting for all shapes using `labelHelper`. The correct approach is to use the shared `getEffectiveHtmlLabels(getConfig())` helper, which correctly resolves both the global and flowchart-scoped settings with proper deprecation handling.

`useHtmlLabels` is being passed as the `addBackground` parameter of `createLabel`. These are semantically distinct: `useHtmlLabels` controls the entire rendering pipeline (HTML vs. SVG), while `addBackground` is a purely visual flag that adds a `labelBkg` CSS class. Conflating them means every terminal edge label will unconditionally receive a background whenever HTML labels are enabled, regardless of the caller's intent. If a background is desired, it should be passed as an explicit boolean (e.g., `true` or a dedicated flag).

The log level was changed from `log.debug` to `log.info` for an internal debug trace (`'vertexText' + vertexText`). This elevates a noisy implementation detail to the `info` level, which is normally reserved for meaningful operational messages. It should remain `log.debug`. Additionally, the string is missing a separator — consider `'vertexText: ' + vertexText`.

`DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH = 200` is defined identically in both `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` and `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js`. Since both files are said to be implementations of the same logic, this constant should live in a shared utility (e.g., a `constants.js`) and be imported in both places to avoid drift.

The `fo.attr('width', 10000).attr('height', 10000)` sentinel value is magic. A named constant (e.g., `LARGE_SENTINEL_SIZE`) with a brief comment explaining why an oversized initial dimension is used (to allow the div to render without clipping before measurement) would improve clarity.

The new `string` branch in `getLabelStyles` is a behavior change worth a comment. Previously, passing a string would have caused `.reduce` to iterate over individual characters (undefined behavior for this use-case); now it is returned directly. While the new behavior is clearly more correct, a short comment explaining why a string might arrive here (and that it is now an accepted type) would help future readers.

general_comments.comment: The PR description states that `createLabel` becomes "a thin wrapper around `createText`", but the actual implementation duplicates the full `addHtmlLabel` rendering pipeline in both `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` — including foreignObject creation, div/span manipulation, bounding-box measurement, and wrapping logic — rather than delegating to `createText`. The stated goal of reducing duplication is not achieved. The two `createLabel` files remain almost identical to each other, and both duplicate logic that already exists in `createText`. Consider having `createLabel` genuinely call `createText` with `{ markdown: false }`, or at minimum extract `addHtmlLabel` into the new `labelImageUtils` module so it is defined only once.

The `addHtmlLabel` function is defined identically (or nearly so) in both `packages/mermaid/src/dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`. Any future bug fix or enhancement must be applied in two places. If a true unification of these files isn't planned, at minimum `addHtmlLabel` should be extracted into the new `labelImageUtils.ts` (or a new shared utility) and imported by both.

The `getWrappingWidth()` helper is defined identically in both `createLabel.js` files but is only used internally within `addHtmlLabel`. Since `addHtmlLabel` now accepts an explicit `width` parameter and falls back to `getWrappingWidth()`, and the callers (e.g., `clusters.js`, `edges.js`) already pass `node.width` or `edge.width`, the helper adds an extra layer of indirection. If the fallback is ever needed, a single shared utility is preferable to two identical private copies.
